newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian Saules says Tallinna Pank to buy shares.
newsitem.headline: Latvian Saules says Tallinna Pank to buy shares.

text.p: Latvian bank Saules Bank said on Monday that one of Estonia's largest banks, Tallinna Pank, is to buy a 20 percent stake in its capital.
"The joining of staff, capital and technological resources is always a positive thing," Saules Bank board member Yuri Shchetinin told Reuters.
He said the deal would take place this year.
Tallinna Pank is the fourth largest commercial bank in Estonia and is following in the footsteps of Estonia's largest bank, Hansapank, which earlier this year also entered the Latvian banking market.
"We have been working on this issue long and thoroughly," Shchetinin added.
The Latvian banking market has this year stabilised after suffering one of eastern Europe's worst bank crises in mid-1995 and has seen increasing internationalisation.
It already has two Western bank branches, Societe Generale and Vereins Bank, and has increasinly become a target for the expansion of Estonian banks.
Estonia is seen as having the most sophisticated banking market in the Baltic states and banks there have been more aggressive in going outside their own borders.
